moat_against: ROIC ~8-9% through the cycle — at/barely above the cost of capital, no wide surplus
Organic growth only 1-3% (FY26 guided) with volume/mix negative (-0.3% Q3 FY26); growth comes from pricing and M&A
Private-label/retailer pressure in a low-switching-cost category
Commodity and freight cost exposure (6-7% cost inflation guided FY26)
Goodwill ~40% of assets — balance sheet carries the acquisition strategy
moat_for: #1 global spices/seasonings position with unmatched retail shelf presence and distribution
Proven pricing power — Q3 FY26 price +2.2% and gross margin +190bp despite 6-7% guided cost inflation
Flavor Solutions B2B embeddedness with packaged-food makers and foodservice
Brand portfolio breadth across consumer and foodservice channels (McCormick, Frank's RedHot, French's, Cholula, Lawry's)
moat_justification: Category-defining brands and demonstrated pricing power (Q3 FY26 price +2.2%, gross margin +190bp), but ROIC ran only 7.2-9.5% across FY2020-FY2025 (fundamentals.json roic_proxy) — at roughly the cost of capital — gross margin is recovering (35.8% FY22 trough to 39.1% TTM) rather than at new highs, organic growth is 1-3% with negative volume/mix, and goodwill is ~40% of assets because growth has been acquired, not compounded.
name: McCormick & Company, Incorporated
one_liner: Durable spice/flavor franchise, moat 5/10, but at $46.35 it doesn't clear 15% on any defensible standalone base (weighted IRR 9.4%, IV@15% $25.55; clears 15% only below ~$26) — and the pending Unilever Foods combination, not standalone DCF value, is what the price is really trading on.
